description.narrative: In 2022, all 11 reports due under ratified Conventions were received by the deadline of 1st September. All reports under ratified Conventions due for 2023 were received by the deadline of 1st September 2023. Three of the four reports requested by the CEACR were received well ahead of deadline, it is only the report on Convention No. 182, which was requested out-of-cycle in June 2023 after the discussion of the application of that Convention by the Committee of Application of Standards of the International Labour Conference, that was received by end of August 2023. This is a significant improvement in relation to previous years, as no reports were received in 2020 and not all of the reports requested were received in 2021. In 2022, the ILO facilitated the recruitment of an international consultant who supported the Government in collecting the relevant information to be included in the reports requested by the CEACR. This included in-depth discussions with the different Government officials and technical entities, on the draft reports and the information to be included in relation to child labour, forced labour, wages, social security, seafarers and dockworkers, among other themes covered by the Conventions for which a report was due. This support resulted in the timely reporting by 1st September 2022, and also significantly helped improve the quality of the reports. This support enhanced the capacity of the Government officials responsible for reporting on Conventions and improved their understanding of the principles and provisions of relevant Conventions. Between March and May 2023, the ILO in collaboration with ITC organised a capacity building workshop on report Writing and facilitated participation of the tripartite partners in the Course on Best Practices in Reporting.

description.narrative: The government of Nigeria ratified 4 ILO Conventions in 2022 and 2023, namely: C190 - Violence and Harassment Convention, 2019 (No. 190); C187 - Promotional Framework for Occupational Safety and Health Convention, 2006 (No. 187); C143 - Migrant Workers (Supplementary Provisions) Convention, 1975 (No. 143); and C181 - Private Employment Agencies Convention, 1997 (No. 181. The aforementioned Conventions were ratified following the relevant recommendation of the National Labour Advisory Council (NLAC) in a meeting held in March 2021. NLAC is the highest tripartite body established by the law on Labour Administration. After the recommendation by the NLAC, the Federal Ministry of Labour held a series of awareness raising workshops on these Conventions in preparation for their ratification as required by law. Thereafter the Conventions were approved for ratification by the Federal Executive Council following a number of meetings in 2022. With funding from the GIZ, ILO supported a gap analysis on C143 and C181 in 2020 which served as the background document for the advocacy for the ratification of both Conventions. In addition, the ILO facilitated the organisation of tripartite awareness raising workshops for both Conventions in March 2022. For Convention 190, the ILO facilitated the organisation of 7 tripartite awareness-raising workshops between September 2021 and September 2022 in Lagos, Abuja, Uyo, Enugu and Keffi, which included presentations on C190. The ILO acted as the resource person at a tripartite workshop held in October 2022 on C187. Additionally, in April 2022, at an advocacy meeting organized by ECOWAS for West Africa, the ILO produced and shared briefing notes on the content of Convention No.190, as well as the benefits of its ratification, to facilitate informed decision-making by stakeholders
